subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the open linked fork fix for sandbox workspace prune cleanup, or close that candidate and allow a fresh narrow repair lane?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and narrow, but the issue is already linked to an open conflicting fork PR, so automated cleanup should not start a competing fix without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt or replace the narrow fix
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source context, but land a current-main OpenClaw PR that safely deletes only stale non-shared sandbox workspaces with focused tests.

options.title: Close the linked fork PR first
options.body: If the fork PR is not salvageable, close it and then allow a fresh narrow fix PR for this issue.

options.title: Defer to broader lifecycle work
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the managed lifecycle PR only if maintainers intentionally want the prune cleanup to ship as part of that broader product change.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the narrow fix
recommendation.body: Use the linked fork PR as source context, but land a current-main OpenClaw PR that safely deletes only stale non-shared sandbox workspaces with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the strongest current-main sandbox history and also opened the broader managed lifecycle follow-up that overlaps this cleanup path.
